lessons.title: More than / less than · 2
lessons.explanation:
plus / moins + [adjective] + que
One frame for every comparison.
lessons.speakingPrompt: Say the example from memory. Then make your own sentence using plus / moins + [adjective] + que.

items.target: Le train est moins rapide que l'avion.
items.native: The train is slower than the plane.
items.note: moins … que = less … than. que becomes qu' before a vowel.

passage.target: Celui-ci est plus cher que celui-là.
passage.native: This one is more expensive than that one.

passage.target: Le train est moins rapide que l'avion.
passage.native: The train is slower than the plane.

lessons.title: The most / very · 2
lessons.objective: the top of a group, or a strong degree
lessons.explanation:
le plus + [adjective] · très / vraiment + [adjective]
French has no ending for "very": it adds feeling with a word.
lessons.speakingPrompt: Say the example from memory. Then make your own sentence using le plus + [adjective] · très / vraiment + [adjective].

items.note: French adds feeling with a word, not an ending: très, vraiment, tellement.

passage.target: C'est le meilleur restaurant de la ville.
passage.native: It is the best restaurant in the city.

lessons.title: Object pronouns · 2
lessons.explanation:
le / la / les · me / te / lui
They sit before the verb, and before an infinitive, never attached to it.
lessons.speakingPrompt: Say the example from memory. Then make your own sentence using le / la / les · me / te / lui.

items.note: Before the infinitive: m'aider = me + aider.

lessons.title: Pour or par · 2
lessons.explanation:
pour vs par
Pour points forward to a goal or a destination; par means by, through or per.
lessons.speakingPrompt: Say the example from memory. Then make your own sentence using pour vs par.

items.target: Prenez ce comprimé deux fois par jour.
items.native: Take this tablet twice a day.
items.note: par + a unit of time = per: deux fois par jour.

passage.target: J'étudie le français pour parler avec mes patients.
passage.native: I study French in order to speak with my patients.

passage.target: Prenez ce comprimé deux fois par jour.
passage.native: Take this tablet twice a day.

lessons.title: Subjunctive after wishes · 2
lessons.objective: wishes, doubts, and requests about someone else
lessons.explanation:
Je veux que / Je souhaite que + [subjunctive]
Two subjects and a wish between them pulls the second verb into the subjunctive. Espérer que is the exception: it takes the indicative.
lessons.speakingPrompt: Say the example from memory. Then make your own sentence using Je veux que / Je souhaite que + [subjunctive].

items.target: Je veux que tu te reposes.
items.note: For most -er verbs the singular subjunctive looks like the present: que tu te reposes.

passage.target: Je souhaite que vous alliez vite mieux.
passage.native: I hope you get better soon.

passage.target: Je veux que tu te reposes.
Je ne pense pas que ce soit grave.
passage.native: I do not think it is serious.

lessons.title: I am (identity) · 3
lessons.explanation:
Je suis + [noun/adjective]
Two words open every self-introduction in French, and a profession needs no article.
lessons.speakingPrompt: Say the example from memory. Then make your own sentence using Je suis + [noun/adjective].

items.note: étudiant en + subject. A woman says étudiante, and the final t is then pronounced.

passage.target: Je suis de l'Idaho, aux États-Unis.
passage.native: I am from Idaho, in the United States.

lessons.title: I have · 3
lessons.objective: I have / I am [age] years old
lessons.explanation:
J'ai + [noun]
Avoir expresses possession AND age — two essentials in one verb.
lessons.speakingPrompt: Say the example from memory. Then make your own sentence using J'ai + [noun].

items.target: J'ai un cabinet à Twin Falls.
items.native: I have a practice in Twin Falls.
items.note: un cabinet (médical) is a doctor's practice; use à before a city name.

passage.target: J'ai un cabinet à Twin Falls.
passage.native: I have a practice in Twin Falls.

lessons.title: I like / I love · 3
lessons.objective: I like [thing] / I like to [do something]
lessons.explanation:
J'aime + [noun / infinitive]
Aimer works like English "like": you are the subject. Add an infinitive, or a noun with le, la or les.
lessons.speakingPrompt: Say the example from memory. Then make your own sentence using J'aime + [noun / infinitive].

items.native: I like to read in the evening.
items.note: le soir = in the evening, with no preposition.

passage.native: I like to read in the evening.

lessons.title: I want to · 3
lessons.explanation:
Je veux + [infinitive]
Je veux + any verb = any desire. The most direct way to say what you want.
lessons.speakingPrompt: Say the example from memory. Then make your own sentence using Je veux + [infinitive].

items.target: Je veux apprendre plus de vocabulaire.
items.native: I want to learn more vocabulary.
items.note: plus de + noun = more of something, with no article after de.

passage.native: I want to speak French fluently.
I want to help my patients.

passage.target: Je veux apprendre plus de vocabulaire.
passage.native: I want to learn more vocabulary.

lessons.title: I have to · 3
lessons.objective: I have to / I must [do something]
lessons.explanation:
Je dois + [infinitive]
Devoir turns every verb you know into an obligation sentence.
lessons.speakingPrompt: Say the example from memory. Then make your own sentence using Je dois + [infinitive].

items.note: je dois and tu dois sound the same; nous devons changes the stem.

passage.target: Je dois opérer à sept heures.
passage.native: I have to perform surgery at seven.

lessons.title: Going to · 3
lessons.explanation:
Je vais + [infinitive]
The near future — simpler than the future tense and used far more in everyday speech.
lessons.speakingPrompt: Say the example from memory. Then make your own sentence using Je vais + [infinitive].

items.target: Qu'est-ce que tu vas faire après ?
items.native: What are you going to do after?
items.note: Qu'est-ce que = what; vas is the tu form of aller.

passage.native: I'm going to explain the procedure.

passage.target: Nous allons arriver à quinze heures.
passage.native: We're going to arrive at three p.m.

passage.target: Qu'est-ce que tu vas faire après ?
passage.native: What are you going to do after?
